title: Integrability of a Gaussian quadratic bound
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, let $v\ge 0$, and let $i,j\in I$. The function $z\mapsto\bigl((z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2\bigr)/(2v^2)+1/v$ is integrable under the product measure whose $k$th coordinate has Gaussian law with mean $c_k$ and variance $v$; at $v=0$, the quotients are interpreted using the usual convention that division by zero is zero.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v\ge0$, and $i,j\in I$. The function $z\mapsto((z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2)/(2v^2)+1/v$ is integrable under $\bigotimes_kN(c_k,v)$, with division by zero interpreted as zero.
